correctness.rationale: Exact one-corner perturbations (4/5,-1/5,1/15,-1/30) yield mass 4/15 per pure coordinate. When n>=8, vertices in distinct corner neighborhoods cannot be adjacent, so each clique sees at most one patch. A complete local pattern check proves every lower clique has nonpositive perturbation and every upper clique stays within its baseline slack. Every clique of the unit-transfer graph lies in a lower or upper clique, so all clique inequalities hold. Five disjoint patches yield the objective C(n+4,4)/5+4/3. The previously proved quinary independence formula then gives a gap at least 8/15. A standalone exact rational checker tests complete graphs at n=8,9,10,11,12,15,20. The infinite proof does not rely on finite tests.

originality.rationale: The new claim is a quantitative, all-degree obstruction specifically to the complete maximal-clique relaxation for quinary unit-transfer graphs. The July 2026 primary full text proves the *integer* optimum and uses larger local tiles; its distinct clique obstruction is at (q,d)=(32,28). The integer value does not imply the existence of the exhibited fractional feasible point, and one isolated distinct obstruction does not imply the present all-n theorem. Actual exact-topic and equivalent-formulation searches produced no covering result. Residual unindexed-priority risk remains.

value.rationale: An all-blocklength impossibility theorem for the strongest possible clique-only fractional upper-bound method in a natural coding channel. The 2026 exact q=5 code theorem requires richer local tiles; this new explicit gap establishes that no rearrangement of maximal-clique inequalities can give sharp bounds for any n>=8, clarifying the mathematical necessity of stronger local inequalities. The additive separation is quantified uniformly and has a short, reusable boundary perturbation proof; no claim of new integer code sizes is made.
